# Profile metrics decision

The README uses two compact SVG cards generated by `.github/scripts/profile_assets.py` and the existing contribution snake. The workflow publishes them to the `output` branch on a daily schedule and after changes to `main`. It uses the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`; no personal access token or custom secret is needed. `contents: write` is required to publish the output branch.

The dashboard reads GitHub GraphQL's contribution calendar and commit contribution count for the last 84 UTC days. Public repository and follower counts come from the GitHub REST user endpoint. The language card sums GitHub Linguist byte counts from public, non-fork repositories. Those percentages describe repository code volume, not personal proficiency or authored code. The cards show public data only; private activity and repositories are outside their scope.

[`lowlighter/metrics`](https://github.com/lowlighter/metrics) was considered for commits, repositories, languages, coding habits, recent activity, and notable contributions. Its [GitHub Action setup](https://github.com/lowlighter/metrics/blob/master/.github/readme/partials/documentation/setup/action.md) asks for a personal token because the repository-scoped `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot access all of its data. Its extra panels would also add height and configuration to this profile. The existing GitHub API script covers the metrics displayed here with fewer dependencies. Streak is omitted because it would require another provider and adds little to the compact dashboard.

The README keeps the role, stack, projects, and contact links in text. If the generated images or the icon service are temporarily unavailable, the essential profile content remains readable. The snake is a visual detail; its published dark and light SVGs were retained.
